r.정치 구도: The king has only a ceremonial role, and the 349-seat parliament chooses the prime minister. Seats are allocated by proportional representation, so many parties win seats, and a center-left bloc and a center-right bloc compete for power. As the Sweden Democrats, who campaign for curbs on immigration, grew, a center-right government propped up by that party from outside took office in 2022. In the September 2026 election the left-leaning bloc won by a razor-thin margin, but the Centre Party, sitting between the blocs, would not commit to either side, and parliament rejected one candidate for prime minister after another. If four votes fail to produce a prime minister, a new election must be held within three months. Rising gang shootings and bombings have made crime and immigration the biggest issues in politics.

t.why: Sweden stayed out of military alliances for more than 200 years after the Napoleonic Wars, but Russia's invasion of Ukraine prompted it to join NATO as the 32nd member in March 2024. Gotland, an island in the middle of the Baltic Sea, sits on the sea's key routes and matters for NATO's defense. It has a defense industry that builds the Gripen fighter jet and is raising military spending quickly. It joined the European Union in 1995, but voters rejected the euro in a 2003 referendum, so it still uses the krona. It awards the Nobel Prizes, and in 1975 it became the first Western country to open an embassy in Pyongyang, where it has looked after US interests in North Korea.
t.rel: It has a long history of cooperation with Norway, Denmark, Finland and Iceland through the Nordic Council, with passport-free travel. It pursued NATO membership together with Finland, and the Oresund Bridge links it with Denmark into a single commuting area. It monitors the Baltic jointly with its neighbors over suspected Russian damage to undersea cables.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1959. When the Korean War broke out, Sweden opened a Red Cross field hospital in Busan in September 1950 and stayed until the spring of 1957, treating soldiers and civilians. In 1958 Sweden, Norway and Denmark founded the National Medical Center in Seoul, continuing that medical support. Since the armistice, Sweden has kept staff at Panmunjom as a member of the Neutral Nations Supervisory Commission. In 1998 Volvo bought Samsung Heavy Industries' construction equipment business and built its Changwon plant into a core excavator production base. In October 2025 Sweden's crown princess and her husband visited Busan to mark the field hospital's 75th anniversary.
t.know: In Jukkasjarvi in the north, a hotel is rebuilt out of ice every winter.
etext: With just over 10 million people, Sweden has produced several world-leading companies in telecom equipment, trucks, industrial machinery and bearings. Its small home market pushed them abroad from the start.
Most of the land is forest, so it sells a lot of timber, pulp and paper. Kiruna in the north is home to Europe's largest iron ore mining, and a rare earths discovery there has drawn attention.
World-class firms have emerged in music streaming, online payments and gaming. Its research and development spending relative to GDP is among the highest in the world.

High house prices and household debt mean consumer spending freezes quickly when interest rates rise. The 2025 bankruptcy of Northvolt, the battery maker that had raised high hopes, showed how hard it is to build new industries.
